(Code 2005, § 26-260; Ord. of 9-3-1991, art. XIII, § 10)
452:
Nothing in this article shall be construed as limiting the right of the County to bring action and seek remedies for environmental hazards and problems other than those hazards and problems enumerated herein. Nothing in this article shall be construed as limiting the types and character of actions and remedies available to the County. The County may exercise and bring any and all of the actions and remedies available under this article and elsewhere independently, concurrently or successively.
(Code 2005, § 26-261; Ord. of 9-3-1991, art. XIII, § 11)
453:
Nothing in this article shall prevent an adjacent or neighboring property owner who would be damaged by a violation, or any other person who would have standing, from bringing a civil action for damages or injunctive relief, to abate a nuisance, for a writ of mandamus or for other appropriate relief.
(Code 2005, § 26-262; Ord. of 9-3-1991, art. XIII, § 12)
456:
(a) Each hearing under this article before the Planning Commission shall be presided over by the Chair thereof, 1 of its members, or any other qualified individual who may be appointed to preside.
(b) Each applicant or permit holder who is a party to a hearing of the Planning Commission under this article shall be entitled to the following rights:
(1) Notice of the date, time, place and purpose of each hearing;
(2) A public hearing;
(3) An impartial tribunal;
(4) To be represented by counsel;
(5) To present evidence and arguments on all issues involved;
(6) To cross examine any witness opposing the applicant or permit holder; and
(7) A ruling based solely on the evidence, the requirements of this article and other lawful considerations.
(c) The Hearing Officer shall not be required to consider or allow immaterial, indecorous or improper matters and conduct.
(d) A written summary of the testimony and arguments shall be prepared by the Hearing Officer or other member of the Planning Commission and signed by the Hearing Officer or Chair.
(e) A record shall be kept of summaries of testimony and arguments, and all notices, documents and official actions.
(f) The Planning Commission shall transmit the record, along with its comments and recommendations, to the Board of Commissioners.
(g) The Board of Commissioners shall consider the record transmitted by the Planning Commission, along with any comments and recommendations of the Planning Commission, and render his ruling, decision or order based upon the same.
(h) The ruling, decision or order of the Board of Commissioners shall be signed by the Chairperson and delivered to the applicant or permit holder by certified mail, return receipt requested.
(i) The Board of Commissioners and the Planning Commission may promulgate additional rules for the implementation of this article.
(j) If the proceeding concerning which the Board of Commissioners has made a ruling, decision or order is quasi-judicial in character, and the applicant or permit holder is dissatisfied therewith, then he may apply for a writ of certiorari to the Superior Court of the County. If the proceeding was legislative, executive or ministerial in character, then the writ shall not lie, and the ruling, decision or order of the Board of Commissioners shall be final and conclusive.
(k) A certified copy of the ruling, decision or order of the Board of Commissioners from which no further review is taken or allowed may be filed in the County Superior Court, whereupon the court shall render judgment in accordance therewith and notify the parties. Such judgment shall have the same effect, and all proceedings in relation thereto shall thereafter be the same, as though such judgment had been rendered in an action duly heard and determined in such Court.
(Code 2005, § 26-281; Ord. of 9-3-1991, art. XIV, § 1)
462:
Any notice under this article, except as otherwise specified, shall be sufficient if deposited in the United States mail, sufficiently addressed, and with sufficient postage thereon to carry same to its destination.
(Code 2005, § 26-321; Ord. of 9-3-1991, art. XVI, § 1)
463:
Any notice mailed to the owner or operator of a facility under the requirements of this article shall be sufficient if mailed to the last-known County address of the facility in the County. If the facility voluntarily discontinues operation in the County with the prior written approval of the Chairperson, then the address shall be sufficient if it is an out-of-County address given to the Chairperson at the time of such voluntary discontinuance.
(Code 2005, § 26-322; Ord. of 9-3-1991, art. XVI, § 2)
466:
This article shall apply to all subject matter that is regulated both by this article and other ordinances, including, but not limited to, ordinances for the development and maintenance of land, and such other ordinances are hereby amended to reflect this. The Board of Commissioners may attach statements to such other ordinances to the effect that compliance with this article is required by such other ordinances.
(Code 2005, § 26-341; Ord. of 9-3-1991, art. XVIII, § 2)
467:
Whenever the provisions and requirements of this article or of any rule, regulation or order pursuant hereto are more restrictive than those under any other statute, law, rule, regulation, ordinance or order of the County, the State or the United States, the provisions and requirements of this article, and the rules, regulations and orders pursuant hereto shall govern to the extent permissible by law. Whenever the provisions of any other statute, law, rule, regulation, ordinance or order of the County, the State or the United States are more restrictive than this article, or any rule, regulation, or order pursuant hereto, then the provisions of such other statute, law, rule, regulation, ordinance or order shall govern.
(Code 2005, § 26-342; Ord. of 9-3-1991, art. XVIII, § 3)
468:
No act or omission of the County, Chairperson, Board of Commissioners or Planning Commission shall be an assurance or guarantee that the United States or any department or agency thereof, or the State or any department or agency thereof, or any other County or any municipality or any department or agency of any other County or of any municipality has taken, is taking, or will take any action or has made, is making or will make any omission. No act or omission of the County, Chairperson, Board of Commissioners or Planning Commission shall be construed as the rendering of advice or an opinion as to the status of legal requirements, policies, acts or omissions of any of the other aforesaid entities.
(Code 2005, § 26-343; Ord. of 9-3-1991, art. XVIII, § 5)
469:
The Governing Authority taking action resulting in adoption of an amendment to this article shall provide for a public hearing on the proposed action. At least 15 but not more than 45 days prior to the date of the hearing, the Governing Authority shall cause to be published within a newspaper of general circulation within the territorial boundaries of the County a notice of the hearing, stating the time, place, and purpose of the hearing.
(Code 2005, § 26-344; Ord. of 9-3-1991, art. XVIII, § 7)
472:
The purpose of this article is to provide for the health, safety, and general welfare of the citizens of Walker County through the regulation of non-stormwater discharges to the storm drainage system to the maximum extent practicable as required by Federal and State law. This article establishes methods for controlling the introduction of pollutants into the municipal separate storm sewer system (MS4) in order to comply with requirements of the National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permit process. The objectives of this article are:
(1) To regulate the contribution of pollutants to the municipal separate storm sewer system (MS4) by stormwater discharges by any user.
(2) To prohibit illicit connections and discharges to the municipal separate storm sewer system.
(3) To establish legal authority to carry out all inspection, surveillance and monitoring procedures necessary to ensure compliance with this article.
(Ord. of 6-24-2004(4), § I)
